name: Pelso Black Sesame-Miso Toffee Shards
manufacturer: Pelso Confections (street brand, Tier 2 district, Ward 14)
description: Hand-poured synth-toffee shards embedded with toasted black sesame and a whisper of white miso, cracked into irregular pieces and wrapped in recycled foil. Pelso makes these in small batches out of a licensed kitchen on Greywater Row, and the inconsistency is part of the appeal.
flavor_profile: Deep, nutty bitterness from black sesame, a slow caramel sweetness that finishes with a savory-umami edge from miso — lingers on the back of the tongue
cultural_context: A cult favorite among Tier 2 factory shift workers who grab a foil packet from corner dispensaries before long overnight runs. The irregular shards make people feel like something was made by hand for them specifically, a rarity in M88.
story_hooks: A runner discovers that certain Pelso foil wrappers have microdot data embedded in them — someone is using the candy supply chain to pass encrypted messages across Ward 14.

The Pelso kitchen is being pressured by a Corponation distributor to standardize production and sell licensing rights — the founder's daughter is trying to find a way to resist without losing everything.
A Tier 4 food critic's anonymous rave review of Pelso shards goes viral on the mesh, and suddenly the street brand can't keep up with demand — and can't afford to scale.
